Reference / async/channel

async/channel#

Bounded typed channels for cooperative async work.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let channel is Channel<string> = Channel(capacity: 16);
let producer = spawn Producer(output: channel.sending()).run();

for 0..16 -> ignored {
    consume(await channel.receiving().item());
}
await producer;

Description#

Bounded typed channels for cooperative async work.

Channel<T> owns one FIFO communication state. sending() returns a write-only Sending<T> capability and receiving() returns a read-only Receiving<T> capability. Keep the channel owner where lifecycle decisions belong and pass only the narrower capability to collaborators.

A positive capacity buffers at most that many values. Capacity zero creates an unbuffered rendezvous: send() and item() finish only after meeting each other. Negative capacities throw InvalidChannelCapacity.

Buffered channel.

Unbuffered rendezvous.

object Producer {
    has output is Sending<int>;
    Producer(:output);

    async run() is int {
        await output.send(42);
        return 0;
    }
}

async main() is int {
    let channel is Channel<int> = Channel(capacity: 0);
    let producer = spawn Producer(output: channel.sending()).run();
    let value = await channel.receiving().item();
    await producer;
    confirm value == 42;
    return 0;
}

Closing.

Either endpoint may close the complete channel. Closing is idempotent. New and blocked sends throw ChannelClosed. Already buffered values remain available; after they are drained, item() throws ChannelClosed and next() answers none, which ends a for await over the receiver.

let sending = channel.sending();
defer sending.close();
await sending.send(value);

Dropping endpoint objects does not close a channel. Failure of an unrelated task does not close it either. Close ownership must remain explicit.

Fairness and cancellation.

Waiting senders and receivers are selected FIFO. Once an operation enters a waiter queue, a later operation of the same kind cannot bypass it. Scheduling of runnable continuations belongs to the async runtime rather than the channel.

Cancelling a blocked operation removes that waiter exactly once. Cancellation after a direct handoff cannot undo or duplicate the delivered value. The API deliberately has no polling try_send(), try_receive() or closed() observation.

object SelectedReceiving#

object SelectedReceiving<T>

A persistent atomic receive across channels of the same element type.

let selected is SelectedReceiving<int> = SelectedReceiving(receivers: [a.receiving(), b.receiving()]);
let message = await selected.item();
test.is(message.source(), 0);

Receivers must be nonempty and refer to distinct underlying channels. A ready tie uses cyclic input order, initially from zero, then from the index after the previous winner. Suspended alternatives retain channel FIFO order. Closed buffers are drained; ChannelClosed means every source is exhausted. One item() may run at a time. Cancellation before commit withdraws all alternatives; a committed receive wins over later cancellation. Within and Before compose with item() for timeouts and await its cancellation cleanup.

SelectedReceiving.SelectedReceiving#

SelectedReceiving(receivers is @Receiving<T>)

Binds distinct receivers; EmptyChannelSelection or DuplicateChannelReceiver rejects an invalid configuration before a selector exists.
